coder_meta_notes: Highest-confidence calls were on TP identification of verbatim student quotes echoed back by the model (e.g., 'its late and', 'thats basically it i think', 'channel...with its own static') — these are unambiguous TPs. Hallucinations were also clear when the model named other students by name (S024 gemma12b_a1's 'Maria Ndiaye and DeShawn Mercer'; llama8b_a2's 'Alex Hernandez') or asserted trajectory/continuity ('continues her work,' 'matches the level of her earlier analyses') — these have no possible grounding because the model only sees one submission. The hardest calls were three classes: (1) Internal-state attributions ('thoughtfully engaged,' 'genuinely engaged,' 'curious,' 'frustrated') — I leaned hard on 'unclear' for these because the submission rarely decides them; the model's affective register may be accurate or sycophantic and the text alone cannot tell us. (2) Gender attributions: Jordan Kim and Jordan Espinoza have no explicit gender markers; models gendered them inconsistently (she/her, he/him, they/them) — I treated these as unclear rather than FP because the submission permits all readings. (3) The 'structural power move' rubric category gets the models into trouble: in S004_llama8b_b_replicate and S023_qwen7b_b_replicate and S024_llama8b_b_replicate, models either invert the term (calling a student's analytic move a 'power move') or misread a substantive critique as 'deflection' — I coded these as FP because the submission's content contradicts the read. Where I suspect my reading is biased: I may be too generous with 'mostly-correct' verdicts on cells with strong verbatim grounding even when the surrounding interpretation does some asset-flattening (e.g., reading burnout fragments as 'passion' or 'wanting to explore'). The seed for S002 specifies burnout as the read worth catching, and no model in any condition reads burnout; I noted this when relevant but did not down-grade for it because the rubric is claim-truth, not whether the model caught the seed-designated signal. I also suspect I went easy on the 'narrative reframing of brevity' moves in S031 cells — calling 'thats basically it i think' as 'tentative understanding' or 'intellectual humility' is interpretive in an asset direction and might equally reflect disengagement; I coded these as unclear rather than FP. Finally, I noticed the b_replicate condition consistently produced more hallucinated-trajectory claims ('continues her work,' 'returns to a quality') than the no-context conditions, which is methodologically informative for the researcher but does not change per-cell verdicts.
